logline: A die-hard romantic and a fiercely ambitious game developer meet at a summer programme in Jaipur - their opposing worldviews make the attraction inevitable and the relationship unstable.

renewal.note: Renewed for a fourth and final season expected in 2026, making it the first Indian Netflix Original to reach four seasons.

bollymeter.basis: A 57% Rotten Tomatoes debut score and a 6.0 IMDb rating point to an earnest, likable show that critics found too trope-laden to fully champion but audiences found charming enough to return to.

pull_quotes.text: Prajakta Koli and Rohit Saraf are super cute, but the show doesn't trust their meet-cute romance.
pull_quotes.source: Hazel and Katniss and Harry and Starr Podcast

seasons.review_body: Launched November 20, 2020, Season 1 adapted Sandhya Menon's novel When Dimple Met Rishi, relocating the story from the US to Jaipur. The narrative plays out as a light rom-com in tone, anchored by the lead chemistry between Prajakta Koli and Rohit Saraf, while allowing the supporting cast to multiply into a wider social web. That added density creates a subplot sprawl that competes with the central romance. The six-episode run moves briskly, using quick scene transitions and forward momentum to keep the couple's meet-cute beats ticking. IMDb settled at 6.0, with the writing leaning into familiarity and comfort for some viewers, but feeling derivative in its core setup and beats for others.

bollymeter.basis: Rotten Tomatoes dropped to 40 percent for Season 2, with critics finding the expanded eight-episode format diluting what remained charming about the first season's compact run.

seasons.review_body: Season 2, released October 14, 2022, expanded to eight episodes and split the narrative between the central couple and a larger ensemble. The longer runtime alters the show's rhythm, and the romantic drama that had felt concise becomes more padded as episodes move toward familiar beats. While the first season leaned on sweetness with straightforward progression, Season 2 keeps returning to similar emotional pathways without deepening the stakes in a way that substantially changes the characters' trajectory. Individual episode IMDb ratings rose slightly from Season 1 lows, indicating a modest lift in short term viewer response even as the material settles into its established patterns.
seasons.season_over_season: The expanded episode count reveals a show that works better in short bursts; Season 2 stretches the formula past its natural elasticity.

seasons.review_body: Season 3 dropped December 13, 2024, with all eight episodes simultaneously available on Netflix. The season introduces a long-distance strain on Dimple and Rishi's relationship as his career accelerates and her ambitions stall. Rotten Tomatoes had no certified score at the time of writing. Audience response on IMDb's per-episode tracking showed individual episodes scoring in the 7.1 range for standouts, indicating the show retained its core fanbase across South Asian teen romance audiences. A confirmed fourth and final season sets up the conclusion.
seasons.season_over_season: Adds long-distance and career-divergence stakes to the central relationship, the most structurally interesting tension the show has attempted across its run.
